span.p: Fastest

span.p: Balanced. The default

span.p: Cheapest

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Start build

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Preset, cap, or level

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Merge, split, reorder, defer

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Why, or can it be cheaper

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Planning starts on its own when discovery is ready
Show the token and dollar or plan-share estimate first
If planning itself would pass the budget, ask first
and offer a cheaper planner level

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
1 System architecture. system-architect, Manager
Components, skeleton data model, inter-feature contracts,
cross-cutting rules with scopes, name prefixes, conventions,
pinned versions, environment manifest
Code checks that every requirement maps, every contract has
a producer and a consumer, and names are unique

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
2 Master plan. master-planner, Manager
Phase 0: everything two or more features consume, plus conventions
Wave order, estimates, paperwork budget per wave
Each shared artifact has exactly one Phase 0 owner

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
3 Feature architecture and planning, just in time per wave
feature-architect and feature-planner, Seniors, in parallel
Flows, screen specs, tasks, visible examples, check slots, one wiring task
3b oracle-author writes the held-back cases, sealed, without the task split

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
4 Graph compile. Kernel
One DAG. No cycles. No two owners of a path or a name. Within size limits
Every requirement has a task and a check. Dependencies are edges

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
5 Estimates. Kernel. Tokens, money or allowance, and time, with ranges
Calibrated history when this developer has it

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
6 Crew proposal. Kernel. Three presets
Each must fit the budget, the connection caps and the machine

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Finished stages stream onto the canvas and can be opened
Cancel is available. A gap reopens only its own criterion

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Phase 0 is a walking skeleton plus the shared contracts
Thinking is done in synthesis, so the tasks are recipes
P0.1 Scaffold runs alone. Junior, low
Then, in parallel where write scopes do not overlap:
P0.2 Packages, one pinned lockfile change. Junior, low
P0.3 Skeleton schema, migration 0001, seed recipe. Mid, or Junior if simple
Feature-only columns arrive later as additive migrations
P0.4 Shared types and validators. Junior, low
P0.5 Auth skeleton, only if two features need it. Mid
P0.6 Test harness and a passing smoke test. Junior, low
P0.7 Tokens, primitives, shell, style guide. Mid
P0.8 .env.example, manifest, CI if requested. Junior, low
Generators make the scaffold mechanical once the decisions exist
An existing repo shrinks Phase 0 to the safety net, the baseline,
shared migrations or types, and extracted conventions

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Foundation gate on harness/integration
Build, lint, smoke test, migration on an empty database,
style guide page renders

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Conventions are quoted into each brief
Lint makes them executable: no new packages outside intents,
no redefining a shared type, no raw colors outside tokens
Shared files belong to the integrator. Workers send an intent

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Feature waves wait. The check goes to the Phase 0 owner
Repeated failure escalates to the Manager

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Level per task, from the planner, checked by code
Rules, contracts, write-scope size, held-back cases,
similar tasks, risk tier
Mechanical is Junior. Standard is Mid
Tricky is Senior. Integration or architecture is Manager
The developer is the CEO

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Critical risk, a very large context,
or a past failure on a similar task?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Bump one level

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Compare expected cost, not the sticker price
Cost per attempt, divided by the chance of passing
A cheap model that often fails can be the expensive one
Start from defaults. Calibrate on this developer's history
Roster maps level to connection, model and effort
It is versioned, because model names change. The sample roster is illustrative

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Workers this wave = the minimum of
ready tasks at once, measured machine slots,
each connection's concurrency cap, the developer's maximum,
and what the budget pace allows
Then critical-path list scheduling: the ready task with the
longest chain behind it, on the best free slot
More workers than the graph's width do not help
Integration cost is why width is also capped
Thinking width and execution width are separate: commands share
a warm pool of 2 to 4 sandboxes. Wrapped agents have a lower cap

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Preset

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Widest. Raise the level of critical-path tasks
Kitchen illustration: 7 peak, about 38 min

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Cheapest level that still meets the pass-rate target
Width limited by pacing. Illustration: 5 peak, about 55 min

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Lowest viable levels. Narrower, to stay inside plan windows
Illustration: 3 peak, about 1 hour 40 min

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Preview: Phase 0, feature waves, crew, time range,
dollar or allowance range, and tasks that rest only
on choices made for you. Peak count changes by wave
A single chain is one worker plus the Manager, and the preview says why
A small machine limits stateful tasks. A low connection cap
limits width, and is named as the reason

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Developer

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The first build of a project always waits for this
Revisions may auto-start: at most 5 tasks, 1 dollar, 2 percent
of a plan window, and no must-ask, breaking contract, destructive
migration, new dependency or external effect. Daily cap 5 dollars
or 10 percent. Otherwise they show a preview

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A request to the owning planner
The preview updates when they republish

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
While building: the hint ladder, then up one level or back to the author
Reschedule when tasks finish early or late
A free worker takes the next ready task
Record class, level, model, tokens, time and pass or fail
A roster change applies to new attempts only
